findings.text: Quota block record carries a field mask plus three resource groups: regular space, inode count, and realtime space. Each group has hard and soft limits, current usage, a grace timer that is zero while inside limits, and warning counters. Timers use signed values while limits and usage use unsigned values.

Quota field selectors occupy single bits 0 through 15. Bits 0 to 5 select inode and space and realtime hard and soft limits and combine into a limit mask. Bits 6 to 8 select timers, bits 9 to 11 select warning counters, bits 12 to 14 select accounting usage, and bit 15 selects flags, each with a combined mask.
Per-type quota state flags use low bits 0 to 3 to record hidden system quota file, root squash, accounting enabled, and limits enforced.

Per-type quota state reports flags, space and inode and realtime grace periods, corresponding warning limits, and quota file identity as inode number plus block and extent counts. Aggregate state reports the number of in-memory quota records plus one per-type entry for every supported quota type.
Quota information update record carries a field mask, state flags, three grace periods for space and inodes and realtime space, and three warning limits for the same resources.

Filesystem quota control is a table of operations bound to a superblock: turn quota on and off, enable and disable by type mask, synchronize, set information, read and step and write per-identity quota blocks, read aggregate state, and remove extended quota by type mask.
Registered quota format entry holds a numeric format identifier, a pointer to format operations, an owning module reference, and a link to the next registered format.

Quota state has three per-type conditions: usage tracking, limit enforcement, and suspended where in-memory information is retained while enforcement is off. Suspended is entered by disabling with the suspended marker and is distinct from fully off.

Internal quota state bits are scaled by quota type count. A last-state position derives from state count times type count, then successive higher bits mark system quota file, permission for negative usage, and exclusion from dirty-list tracking. A combined value covers the three base state flags.

Per-type flag helpers shift a generic flag set left by quota type to test one type, shift right and mask to recover the generic set, and divide by a single-bit flag and mask to return a bitmask of types carrying that condition. The type-extraction helper only accepts a power-of-two selector.
Warning notification helper accepts an identity, device, and warning kind and performs no action in the routed configuration.
Per-superblock quota context holds option flags, one quota-file inode pointer per quota type, one in-memory information record per type, and one format operations pointer per type.
Per-superblock quota context serializes quota file input and output with a read-write semaphore held across I/O, separate from the plain flags and per-type arrays.
Quota module table maps old and current VFS quota format identifiers to owning module names, terminated by a zero identifier with a null name.
Space accounting mode uses bit 0 for warn, bit 1 for reservation without immediate inode byte change, and bit 2 for no-fail allocation.
Superblock quota accessor returns the address of the embedded quota context, and the per-type accessor returns the address of the indexed per-type information entry.
Attribute change counts as quota-relevant when size is being set or when owner or group identity requires an update under the mount identity mapping.
Quota error reporting helper forwards superblock, format, and arguments plus the caller's function name to a common error routine.
A quota record is considered busy when its modified marker is set or when its reference count is positive.

Enabled-build superblock queries test shifted usage, limit, and suspended markers per type. Loaded means usage is enabled, active means loaded and not suspended, and aggregate queries return type bitmasks for suspended and loaded states.
Disabled-build quota state queries always report absent or inactive, including per-type usage, limits, suspended, loaded, active, and aggregate loaded and suspended checks.

Disabled-build quota lifecycle and transfer helpers always succeed or do nothing: initialization reports success and never needed, drop and inode free do nothing, inode allocation and ownership transfer report success, and disable, suspend, resume, and writeback report success.
Disabled-build quota file open is defined as the generic file open operation.

Disabled-build space helpers maintain inode byte counts directly: reservation mode skips byte adjustment while non-reservation allocation and release adjust bytes, and claim and reclaim helpers always adjust bytes with reclaim reporting success.

Block and space wrapper family converts block counts using the inode block-size shift, selects warning, reservation, and no-fail modes, and applies three dirtying disciplines: leave clean, mark synchronously dirty, or mark fully dirty after successful allocation.
Disabled-build allocation paths do not enforce limits and only adjust usage counters, so success from those wrappers must not be read as quota admission.
Memory filesystem no-MMU mapping expansion helper unconditionally reports success for the supplied inode and size.

Sequential file state holds a growable output buffer with size and fill and read offsets, padding target, iteration index and read position, owning operations and file pointers, poll event marker, and private context. Its operations table provides start, stop, next, and show callbacks over opaque iteration values.
Sequential file state contains a mutex that serializes traversal and output generation across concurrent readers of the same instance.
Sequential file show callback uses value one to request skipping the current entry, and iteration uses a small nonzero sentinel pointer to mark the start position.

Sequential file helper macros generate an open routine plus file or proc operations binding read and seek to shared sequential handlers with the matching release handler. The plain sequential form opens supplied operations and inherits inode private data, single-shot forms bind a show callback with inode or proc private data, and the store form additionally binds a write callback.

Mount option display helper prefixes a comma, escapes separator and whitespace characters in the name, and when a value exists adds an equals sign followed by the escaped value. The counted variant copies a fixed-length value into a terminated temporary before display.

Kernel status record reports result mask, mode, link count, preferred I/O size, attribute value and mask, inode and device identities, owner and group, size, four timestamps including creation time, block count, mount identity, change cookie, subvolume, direct-I/O alignment values, and atomic write size and segment limits.

Permission group combinations cover all users, groups, and others for read, write, execute, and full access plus set-uid, set-gid, and sticky bits. Timestamp sentinels request current time and omission using adjacent large values below a power-of-two boundary.
Extended status uses one high flag to request or report a change attribute and the top attribute bit to promise that the version increases monotonically.

Status attribute masks separate filesystem ioctl-backed attributes covering compression, immutability, append-only, no-dump, encryption, and verity from VFS-enforced immutability and append-only flags.
Filesystem status record reports type, block sizes, total and free and available blocks, total and free file slots, filesystem identity, maximum name length, mount flags, and spare fields.

Filesystem mount status flags mark read-only, no set-uid, no devices, no execution, synchronous writes, supported flags, mandatory locking, no access-time updates, no directory access-time updates, relative access-time updates, and no symlink following.
Sysfs attribute descriptor carries a name and mode, plus lock-class tracking fields when lock allocation debugging is enabled.

Sysfs attribute initialization either assigns a private lock-class key or does nothing, depending on lock debugging configuration. The alternative-member helper selects either structure or union layout depending on configuration.
Busy-state finding relies on reference-count read owned elsewhere.
Busy-state finding relies on bit test owned elsewhere.
Type-extraction finding relies on power-of-two build check owned elsewhere.
